\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{کلاهبرداری} (kolâhbardâri)}{کلاهبرداری (kolâhbardâri)}]{\fa{کلاهبرداری} (kolâhbardâri) — fraud, a scam}

\label{lesson:FA-C408-kolahbardari}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for innocent, then the Persian for to sentence.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{کلاهبرداری}}
\textbf{\fa{کلاهبرداری}} (\emph{kolâhbardâri}) — \textquotedblleft{}fraud, a scam\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{این} \fa{ایمیل} \fa{یک} \fa{کلاهبرداری} \fa{است}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{in imeyl yek kolâhbardâri ast.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
This email is a scam.
\end{quote}

Literally hat-lifting: \emph{kolâh} \textquotedblleft{}hat\textquotedblright{} + \emph{bardâri} \textquotedblleft{}taking up\textquotedblright{}. \emph{Kolâhbardâr} — a swindler.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{کلاهبرداری}} is a native Persian compound built from \emph{kolâh} \textquotedblleft{}hat\textquotedblright{}, which EtymDB traces to Middle Persian \emph{kulāf}, + \emph{bardâri} \textquotedblleft{}lifting\textquotedblright{}, from \emph{bar} \textquotedblleft{}up\textquotedblright{} and \emph{dâshtan} \textquotedblleft{}to hold\textquotedblright{}. A swindler lifts your hat.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kolâhbardâri}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{kolâhbardâri}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{kolâhbardâri}
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Persian for innocent, then the Persian for to sentence, then say \emph{kolâhbardâri} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \fa{کلاهبرداری} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Fraud, a scam\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{سرقت} (serqat)}{سرقت (serqat)}]{\fa{سرقت} (serqat) — theft, robbery}

\label{lesson:FA-C408-serqat}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for to sentence, then the Persian for fraud.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{سرقت}}
\textbf{\fa{سرقت}} (\emph{serqat}) — \textquotedblleft{}theft, robbery\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{دیشب} \fa{در} \fa{محله} \fa{ما} \fa{یک} \fa{سرقت} \fa{اتفاق} \fa{افتاد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{dishab dar mahalle-ye mâ yek serqat ettefâq oftâd.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Last night there was a robbery in our neighbourhood.
\end{quote}

The formal word; everyday speech says \emph{dozdi}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{سرقت}} is usually traced to Arabic \emph{sariqa} \textquotedblleft{}theft\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{رشوه} (reshve)}{رشوه (reshve)}]{\fa{رشوه} (reshve) — a bribe}

\label{lesson:FA-C408-reshve}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for fraud, then the Persian for theft.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{رشوه}}
\textbf{\fa{رشوه}} (\emph{reshve}) — \textquotedblleft{}a bribe\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{رشوه} \fa{نگرفت}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u reshve nagereft.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He did not take a bribe.
\end{quote}

\emph{Reshve dâdan / gereftan} — to give / take a bribe.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{رشوه}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{rashwa} \textquotedblleft{}a bribe\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{فساد} (fesâd)}{فساد (fesâd)}]{\fa{فساد} (fesâd) — corruption}

\label{lesson:FA-C408-fesad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for theft, then the Persian for a bribe.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{فساد}}
\textbf{\fa{فساد}} (\emph{fesâd}) — \textquotedblleft{}corruption\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{مردم} \fa{از} \fa{فساد} \fa{خسته} \fa{شده} \fa{اند}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{mardom az fesâd khaste shode and.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
People are tired of corruption.
\end{quote}

Also decay: \emph{fesâd-e mive}, fruit going bad.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{فساد}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{fasād} \textquotedblleft{}corruption, decay\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\fa{اتهام} (ettehâm)}{اتهام (ettehâm)}]{\fa{اتهام} (ettehâm) — a charge, an accusation}

\label{lesson:FA-C408-etteham}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Persian for a bribe, then the Persian for corruption.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \fa{اتهام}}
\textbf{\fa{اتهام}} (\emph{ettehâm}) — \textquotedblleft{}a charge, an accusation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\fa{او} \fa{این} \fa{اتهام} \fa{را} \fa{قبول} \fa{نکرد}.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{u in ettehâm râ qabul nakard.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He did not accept this accusation.
\end{quote}

Plural \emph{ettehâmât}. \emph{Be ettehâm-e} … — on a charge of … .

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\fa{اتهام}} was borrowed from Arabic \emph{ittihām} \textquotedblleft{}accusation\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}
